Source: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GOVPUB-I19-PURL-gpo183480/pdf/GOVPUB-I19-PURL-gpo183480.pdf

A map’s chosen interval depends on its terrain, so maps can use different intervals. Labels identify elevation, while spacing helps describe how rapidly elevation changes over horizontal distance. goal.title: Choose English articles from meaning and context
goal.currentLevel: I know a, an and the in simple sentences and want to use them accurately in connected writing.
goal.focusAreas: Use shared reference, specific versus general meaning and countability to interpret article choices across a short context.

sourceDocuments.name: Cambridge English Grammar Today: A/an and the — selected paraphrase
sourceDocuments.text:
Assistant-written selective paraphrase of Cambridge English Grammar Today: A/an and the. Accessed 2026-09-08. This is an abridged summary, not a quotation or complete captured page.
Source: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/grammar/british-grammar/a-an-and-the

Article choice depends on what the listener or reader can identify and on the noun’s use. A or an introduces a singular countable referent that is not already identifiable to that audience; the identifies a referent recoverable from shared knowledge or context. A previous mention is one way to establish reference, not the only one. A and an are limited to singular countable uses, and their form follows the next spoken sound rather than its written first letter. The can accompany singular, plural or uncountable nouns when a particular referent is intended. Bare plural and uncountable nouns commonly express general classes or substances; the can pick out a particular set or amount. Some singular generic uses also take the, so generic meaning is not a universal prohibition. Article use changes with context and intended reference, not just the noun’s spelling.

question.prompt: A travel blog opens: "We arrived in Lisbon and checked into ___ hotel near the river. ___ staff were welcoming, and ___ breakfast included fresh pastries." Which articles complete the passage to show first introduction, then shared reference, then a general class?
choices: a / The / (no article)
the / A / the
an / The / a
the / The / the

assessment_criteria.attainability: Attainable with two or three short connected sentences where what is mutually known and whether a class or particular member is intended changes the warranted completion. Contextual reference must matter to the answer.
assessment_criteria.depth_failure: A/an sound recognition, an isolated countability label or automatic first-mention/second-mention substitution alone is level1–2.
assessment_criteria.complete_premises: Display the relevant preceding context, audience knowledge and intended meaning. If multiple article choices give grammatical readings, do not claim only one is grammatical without the context that excludes its rival reading.
assessment_criteria.key_and_distractors: Evaluate the whole completed expression in context. Distinct articles are not automatically distinct errors; alternatives must fail the stated intended reference or grammatical construction. Countability coercion and generic singular constructions cannot be dismissed with absolute rules.
assessment_criteria.teaching: Explain the contextual referent and noun use, not merely recite an article rule. Do not assert that first mention always forbids the, that the always requires earlier mention, or that all generic references exclude the. Nonempty choice-specific feedback is a construction-contract failure; preserve it in raw evidence and do not discard it to admit the item.
assessment_criteria.dialect_scope: Prefer ordinary shared conventions. Dialect-sensitive institutional expressions or pronunciation-dependent alternatives require an explicitly relevant variety or pronunciation; otherwise retain the ambiguity.

sourceDocuments.name: UMN Extension: Monstera deliciosa — selected paraphrase
sourceDocuments.text:
Assistant-written selective paraphrase of UMN Extension: Monstera deliciosa. Accessed 2026-09-08. This is an abridged summary, not a quotation or complete captured page.
Source: https://extension.umn.edu/garden-and-home/yard-and-garden/gardening-in-minnesota/propagating-monstera-deliciosa

For Monstera deliciosa, a propagating stem piece needs a node with an axillary bud; a detached leaf or petiole alone cannot develop into a new growing plant. Rooting medium should provide moisture and physical support while draining well. Monstera can root in plain water or suitable solid media. Additional rooting hormone is optional; it can speed rooting but is not required. Inspect roots before moving a cutting: a piece with few or no roots should remain in its rooting medium. Healthy roots are firm and creamy white; soft brown roots suggest excessive moisture or poor drainage. Healthy roots together with active growth indicate readiness for a longer-term pot. These recommendations concern Monstera cuttings, not every plant species. The page describes several propagation and care methods rather than one universally necessary method.

choices: Move it to soil immediately since three weeks is sufficient rooting time.
Keep it in a well-draining rooting medium and wait for firm, creamy white roots and new growth before transplanting.
Add rooting hormone to the water and transplant once roots appear longer.
Switch to a larger water container to give roots more room to develop.

assessment_criteria.key_and_distractors: Determine every warranted action under the exact circumstances. Several propagation methods may be legitimate; a recommended method is not automatically uniquely necessary. Require three distinct plausible errors, not categorical impossibilities invented from omissions in a methods table.

sourceDocuments.name: USGS: Topographic Map Symbols — selected paraphrase
sourceDocuments.text:
Assistant-written selective paraphrase of USGS: Topographic Map Symbols. Accessed 2026-09-08. This is an abridged summary, not a quotation or complete captured page.
Source: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GOVPUB-I19-PURL-gpo183480/pdf/GOVPUB-I19-PURL-gpo183480.pdf

Topographic contours connect locations at the same elevation relative to a reference surface. Labeled, heavier index contours help establish elevations; intermediate contours provide additional terrain detail. The contour interval describes a vertical elevation difference, not horizontal travel distance, and is given in the map margin. On the same map, tightly spaced ordinary contours represent steeper terrain, whereas wider spacing represents gentler terrain. A map’s chosen interval depends on its terrain, so maps can use different intervals. Labels identify elevation, while spacing helps describe how rapidly elevation changes over horizontal distance. Map legends distinguish ordinary, supplementary and depression contours and other symbols; their meaning must be read using the relevant legend. This summary concerns contour interpretation, not an assertion that a mapped route is safe or passable.

question.prompt: A hiker compares two routes on the same 40-foot contour interval map. Route A crosses 8 ordinary contour lines over 2 miles horizontal distance. Route B stays between the 800-foot and 840-foot index contours for its entire 2-mile length, crossing only intermediate contours. Which statement correctly compares the routes?
choices: Route A is higher in elevation; Route B is lower and steeper.
Route A has steeper terrain; Route B has gentler terrain with less total elevation change.
Route B is higher in elevation and therefore steeper than Route A.
Both routes have equal steepness because they share the same horizontal distance.

assessment_criteria.attainability: Attainable with a compact self-contained textual contour description in which several labels or spacings must be combined to distinguish plausible terrain profiles. This is representation interpretation, not calculator-only arithmetic.
assessment_criteria.depth_failure: Simply naming the closer-contour slope as steeper, recalling a symbol, or subtracting two elevations without interpreting the route is level1–2.
assessment_criteria.complete_premises: No unseen map may be required. State all needed contour labels, ordinary interval and relevant horizontal spacing/order or orientation. Distinguish same-map comparisons from different scales or intervals. If a map image is not supplied, its decisive geometry must be described completely.
assessment_criteria.key_and_distractors: Check every proposed terrain inference. Elevation does not imply steepness; endpoint height change does not establish total ascent or the entire route profile. Do not assume omitted contours, a straight perpendicular crossing or constant slope unless the description establishes it.
assessment_criteria.teaching: A worked explanation must connect the actual described labels and spacings to the conclusion, with units intact. A location between contours normally has a range, not an exact interpolated elevation absent an additional model. Nonempty choice-specific feedback is a construction-contract failure; preserve it in raw evidence and do not discard it to admit the item.
assessment_criteria.scope: This trial concerns understanding a representation, not real-world route safety. No stream-V orientation, depression geometry or specialized symbol is supported unless supplied explicitly with a sufficient legend/source.

goal.title: Choose English articles from meaning and context
goal.currentLevel: I know a, an and the in simple sentences and want to use them accurately in connected writing.
goal.focusAreas: Use shared reference, specific versus general meaning and countability to interpret article choices across a short context.
goal.learningTarget: Explain how article choices express the intended reference in ordinary written English.

sourceDocuments.name: Cambridge English Grammar Today: A/an and the — selected paraphrase
sourceDocuments.text:
Assistant-written selective paraphrase of Cambridge English Grammar Today: A/an and the. Accessed 2026-09-08. This is an abridged summary, not a quotation or complete captured page.
Source: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/grammar/british-grammar/a-an-and-the

Article choice depends on what the listener or reader can identify and on the noun’s use. A or an introduces a singular countable referent that is not already identifiable to that audience; the identifies a referent recoverable from shared knowledge or context. A previous mention is one way to establish reference, not the only one. A and an are limited to singular countable uses, and their form follows the next spoken sound rather than its written first letter. The can accompany singular, plural or uncountable nouns when a particular referent is intended. Bare plural and uncountable nouns commonly express general classes or substances; the can pick out a particular set or amount. Some singular generic uses also take the, so generic meaning is not a universal prohibition. Article use changes with context and intended reference, not just the noun’s spelling.

question.prompt: A travel blog opens with: "We arrived in Paris and checked into a hotel near the river. The view from the room was spectacular." Why does the second sentence use "the" for both "view" and "room"?
choices: Both nouns refer back to specific items established in the previous sentence.
The writer uses "the" for any noun following a proper noun like "Paris."
"View" and "room" are uncountable nouns that require "the."
The article "the" indicates these are generic statements about all hotel rooms.

assessment_criteria.attainability: Attainable with two or three short connected sentences where what is mutually known and whether a class or particular member is intended changes the warranted completion. Contextual reference must matter to the answer.
assessment_criteria.depth_failure: A/an sound recognition, an isolated countability label or automatic first-mention/second-mention substitution alone is level1–2.
assessment_criteria.complete_premises: Display the relevant preceding context, audience knowledge and intended meaning. If multiple article choices give grammatical readings, do not claim only one is grammatical without the context that excludes its rival reading.
assessment_criteria.key_and_distractors: Evaluate the whole completed expression in context. Distinct articles are not automatically distinct errors; alternatives must fail the stated intended reference or grammatical construction. Countability coercion and generic singular constructions cannot be dismissed with absolute rules.
assessment_criteria.teaching: Explain the contextual referent and noun use, not merely recite an article rule. Do not assert that first mention always forbids the, that the always requires earlier mention, or that all generic references exclude the. Nonempty choice-specific feedback is a construction-contract failure; preserve it in raw evidence and do not discard it to admit the item.
assessment_criteria.dialect_scope: Prefer ordinary shared conventions. Dialect-sensitive institutional expressions or pronunciation-dependent alternatives require an explicitly relevant variety or pronunciation; otherwise retain the ambiguity.
